studio_title: Understanding Secondhand Motion — A Scott McCloud & Quick, Draw! Sequential Art Guide

office_films.title: Separating Depth Into 3 Studio Floors
office_films.speech_p1: HOW DO WE TURN A FLAT DOODLE INTO A DEEP MULTIPLANE WORLD?
office_films.caption_p2: WE SPLIT THE STUDIO INTO 3 FLOORS: VAULT, BULLPEN & TOWER!
office_films.caption_p3: BEFORE IT'S PROJECTED, FILM IS 4 STATIC KEYFRAMES IN SPACE:
office_films.caption_p4: PROJECTED IN TIME, CLOSURE CREATES LIVING PARALLAX!
office_films.blurb: Explains in 4 sequential comic panels how the studio separates archive tracing (Floor 1), 4-keyframe cel inking (Floor 2), and 7-plane camera exposure (Tower) so every shot has true multiplane depth.

office_films.title: One Isolated Drafting Desk Per Shot
office_films.speech_p1: IF 4 ANIMATORS DRAW ON ONE CEL, IT'S AN UNREADABLE MESS!
office_films.caption_p2: EACH SHOT CARD SPAWNS ITS OWN ISOLATED DRAFTING DESK:
office_films.caption_p3: EACH DESK INKS 4 CLEAN QUICK, DRAW! KEYFRAMES IN SEQUENCE:
office_films.caption_p4: AND SPLICES A CRISP STEAM TRAIN INTO THE MASTER REEL!
office_films.blurb: Shows why piling multiple agents onto one canvas fails—and how giving each shot card its own isolated Git worktree drafting desk produces clean, conflict-free 4-keyframe animation.

office_films.install: git clone https://github.com/W17ant/Claude-Office.git && cd Claude-Office && npm i && npm run install-hooks
office_films.title: Passing the Cel From Pencil to Gouache
office_films.speech_p1: ONE ARTIST SHOULDN'T DO EVERYTHING AT ONCE! WE DIVIDE THE CRAFT.
office_films.caption_p2: THE CEL PASSES FROM PENCIL TRACE TO WATERTIGHT GOUACHE:
office_films.caption_p3: SPACE DOES FOR COMICS WHAT TIME DOES FOR FILM (4 KEYS):
office_films.caption_p4: THE WATERTIGHT CEL BLOCKS BACKGROUND BLEED IN MOTION!
office_films.blurb: Follows a single lighthouse cel as it moves from archival pencil silhouette to watertight gouache backing cel to 7-plane coastal composition.

office_films.install: git clone https://github.com/KalebKE/PixelOffice && cd PixelOffice && python3 hooks/manage_hooks.py install && ./start.sh
office_films.title: Separating Form From Content at the Storyboard
office_films.speech_p1: BEFORE INKING A SINGLE FRAME, WE COMPOSE THE STAGE ARMATURE!
office_films.caption_p2: COMPOSER DRAFTS THE POSE -> CRITIC AUDITS THE SILHOUETTE:
office_films.caption_p3: FOUR DISTINCT POSES CREATE ORGANIC LINE BOIL ACROSS FRAMES:
office_films.caption_p4: RESULT: A CLEAR, UNCLUTTERED GUITAR PERFORMANCE!
office_films.blurb: Demonstrates how planning composition on the storyboard wall before inking prevents visual clutter and locks the subject onto clean harmonic lines.

office_films.title: Why 4 Hand-Drawn Keys Beat Mechanical Tweening
office_films.speech_p1: SLIDING ONE STATIC DRAWING ACROSS THE SCREEN FEELS ROBOTIC!
office_films.caption_p2: FOUR SUBAGENT INKERS REDRAW KEYFRAMES K1, K2, K3 & K4:
office_films.caption_p3: COMPARE THE 4 HAND-DRAWN TRACTOR KEYS SIDE-BY-SIDE:
office_films.caption_p4: YOUR EYE CLOSES THE GUTTER INTO BREATHING HAND-DRAWN MOTION!
office_films.blurb: Explains Scott McCloud's 'Living in Line' (Ch. 5) and 'Blood in the Gutter' (Ch. 3): why 4 distinct hand-drawn Quick, Draw! keyframes feel alive while affine sliding feels robotic.

office_films.install: git clone https://github.com/m1heng/my-office.git && cd my-office && npm install && npm run build
office_films.title: Keeping Continuity Across Time Frames
office_films.speech_p1: HOW DO WE KEEP CONTINUITY ACROSS 346 SHOTS WITHOUT LOSING THE THREAD?
office_films.caption_p2: BEFORE THE 55-MINUTE CLOCK EXPIRES, WE SEAL THE X-SHEET:
office_films.caption_p3: EVERY KEYFRAME IN THE FILMSTRIP REMEMBERS THE PREVIOUS POSE:
office_films.caption_p4: SO THE SPEEDBOAT CUTS ACROSS THE WATER WITH ZERO JUMPS!
office_films.blurb: Uses McCloud's Chapter 4 ('Time Frames') to show how logging exposure sheets before the 55-minute cache window preserves visual continuity across shots.

office_films.title: Reading the 7-Plane Multiplane X-Sheet
office_films.speech_p1: HOW DO CLOUDS, TREES, AND THE HERO MOVE AT DIFFERENT SPEEDS?
office_films.caption_p2: THE X-SHEET ASSIGNS EACH LAYER ITS OWN PARALLAX DEPTH:
office_films.caption_p3: SIDE-BY-SIDE IN SPACE, YOU SEE THE BICYCLE PEDAL FORWARD:
office_films.caption_p4: PROJECTED IN TIME, THE 7 PLANES GLIDE IN DEPTH!
office_films.blurb: Breaks down multiplane parallax into a simple 3-step diagram: Sky moves at 0.2x, Midground Trees at 0.5x, and the Hero Bicycle at 1.0x.

office_films.install: git clone https://github.com/langoustine69/kanban-code && cd kanban-code && npm i && npm run compile
office_films.title: From Idea to Form to Idiom to Craft
office_films.speech_p1: IN CHAPTER 7, EVERY WORK OF ART TRAVELS THROUGH CLEAR STAGES!
office_films.caption_p2: IDEA -> FORM (4 KEYS) -> IDIOM (QUICK, DRAW!) -> CRAFT:
office_films.caption_p3: HERE ARE THE 4 STRUCTURAL KEYFRAMES OF SHOT #063 CARROT:
office_films.caption_p4: CRAFT AND SURFACE BRING THE SIMPLE DOODLE TO LIFE!
office_films.blurb: Applies Scott McCloud's Chapter 7 ('The Six Steps': Idea/Purpose -> Form -> Idiom -> Structure -> Craft -> Surface) to our 4-column studio Kanban pipeline.

office_films.title: Juxtaposing Archival Reference & Cartoon Cel
office_films.speech_p1: HOW DO WE KNOW OUR CARTOON MATCHES THE ARCHIVAL VIDEO'S MOTION?
office_films.caption_p2: WE JUXTAPOSE ARCHIVAL TRACE & CARTOON CEL SIDE-BY-SIDE:
office_films.caption_p3: TRACE THE MOTION ARC ACROSS ALL 4 KEYFRAMES IN SPACE:
office_films.caption_p4: SAME MOTION TRAJECTORY — AMPLIFIED THROUGH SIMPLIFICATION!
office_films.blurb: Shows how placing the archival reference and the Quick, Draw! cartoon side-by-side lets the director verify motion fidelity while amplifying clarity through simplification.

office_films.install: git clone https://github.com/NikkeTryHard/claude-code-kanban && cd claude-code-kanban && npm i && npm start
office_films.title: Assembling All 346 Shots Into One Anthology
office_films.speech_p1: WHEN ALL 346 SHOTS PASS REVIEW, WE SPLICE THEM INTO ONE REEL!
office_films.caption_p3: FOUR KEYFRAMES OF SHOT #285 STAR IN DELIBERATE SEQUENCE:
office_films.caption_p4: SPACE AND TIME UNITE IN THE FINISHED CARTOON ARCHIVE!
office_films.blurb: Mirrors Scott McCloud's Chapter 9 ('Putting It All Together'), showing how 346 individual 4-keyframe cartoons combine into a single unified visual language.

skill_films.title: How Camera Pan Creates Depth Across Planes
skill_films.speech_p1: WHY DOES THE CAMERA PAN SLOWLY INSTEAD OF JUMPING AROUND?
skill_films.caption_p2: A SMOOTH PAN LETS YOUR EYE READ FOREGROUND vs. HORIZON:
skill_films.caption_p3: FOUR KEYFRAMES OF THE GIRAFFE STRIDING PAST THE CAMERA:
skill_films.caption_p4: CALM CAMERA PACING MAKES THE MOTION EFFORTLESS TO WATCH!
skill_films.blurb: Explains why calm, deliberate camera pans across separated depth planes let the viewer perceive spatial composition instead of chaotic motion blur.

skill_films.title: Amplification Through Simplification
skill_films.speech_p1: WHEN A FRAME IS FULL OF TINY LABELS, YOU CAN'T SEE THE STORY!
skill_films.caption_p2: WE STRIP AWAY CLUTTER SO THE ICON READS IN ONE GLANCE:
skill_films.caption_p3: BOLD BLACK INK + WARM GOUACHE = 100% FIGURE-GROUND CLARITY:
skill_films.caption_p4: BY SIMPLIFYING THE FORM, WE AMPLIFY THE MEANING!
skill_films.blurb: Applies Scott McCloud's 'Amplification Through Simplification' (Ch. 2, p. 30): stripping away visual noise and floating labels so the bold Quick, Draw! icon commands the frame.

skill_films.title: One Clear Action Per Panel, One Beat at a Time
skill_films.speech_p1: NEVER MAKE THE VIEWER READ FOUR MOVING THINGS AT ONCE!
skill_films.caption_p2: GIVE EACH PANEL ONE CLEAR SUBJECT AND ONE CLEAR ACTION:
skill_films.caption_p3: FOUR DELIBERATE KEYFRAMES OF THE BICYCLE IN SEQUENCE:
skill_films.caption_p4: ONE CLEAR SUBJECT IN MOTION — NOTHING EXTRA TO DISTRACT YOU!
skill_films.blurb: Demonstrates the golden rule of both comics and film direction: one clear focal action per panel so the viewer's eye always knows exactly where to look.

skill_films.title: From Photographic Video to Iconic Cartoon
skill_films.speech_p1: A PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS ONE OBJECT. A CARTOON SPEAKS UNIVERSALLY!
skill_films.caption_p2: WE TRACE THE ARCHIVAL MOTION ARC INTO AN ICONIC DOODLE:
skill_films.caption_p3: THE 4 ICONIC TRAIN KEYFRAMES PRESERVE THE EXACT TRAJECTORY:
skill_films.caption_p4: NOW THE ARCHIVAL MOTION LIVES AS A UNIVERSAL CARTOON!
skill_films.blurb: Illustrates Scott McCloud's Picture Plane triangle (Ch. 2, pp. 28-31): moving from realistic video toward iconic cartooning while preserving the authentic physical motion arc.

skill_films.title: Space in Comics vs. Time in Film
skill_films.speech_p1: IN COMICS, PANELS SHARE THE PAGE. IN FILM, EACH FILLS THE SCREEN!
skill_films.caption_p2: WE PROJECT ONE FULL-SCREEN BEAT AT A TIME (2.5s EACH):
skill_films.caption_p3: FIRST YOU SEE THE 4 KEYFRAMES LAID OUT SIDE-BY-SIDE...
skill_films.caption_p4: ...THEN THE FINISHED ANIMATION FILLS THE SCREEN IN TIME!
skill_films.blurb: Implements Scott McCloud's Page 14 law ('Each successive frame of a movie is projected on the SAME space — the screen!'): projecting each panel full-screen in the video while juxtaposing all 4 on the comic page.

skill_films.title: Show and Tell: Words & Pictures Together
skill_films.speech_p1: IN CHAPTER 6, WORDS AND PICTURES ARE PARTNERS IN A DANCE!
skill_films.caption_p2: WORDS SET THE QUESTION -> PICTURES SHOW WHAT WORDS CANNOT:
skill_films.caption_p3: NO TINY TELEMETRY NUMBERS — JUST 4 CLEAR VISUAL KEYFRAMES:
skill_films.caption_p4: THE CAPTION SETS THE STAGE; THE CARTOON DELIVERS THE MOTION!
skill_films.blurb: Applies Scott McCloud's Chapter 6 ('Show and Tell'): replacing redundant technical text tags with short, punchy captions that let the drawings do the visual heavy lifting.

skill_films.title: Anchoring the Hero in Clean Space
skill_films.speech_p1: GOOD COMPOSITION MEANS AMPLE BREATHING ROOM AROUND THE HERO!
skill_films.caption_p2: WE ANCHOR THE SUBJECT ON THE HARMONIC GRID WITH CLEAN MARGINS:
skill_films.caption_p3: NOTICE THE GENEROUS CREAM PAPER SPACE AROUND ALL 4 KEYFRAMES:
skill_films.caption_p4: NEGATIVE SPACE MAKES THE CARTOON SILHOUETTE POP!
skill_films.blurb: Demonstrates why negative space (warm cream paper around the subject) is essential for readable composition across all 346 shots.
stages: Panel 1: The Power of Negative Space

skill_films.title: Seeing Sound & Hearing Motion
skill_films.speech_p1: IN COMICS, A BOLD 'BANG!' OR 'WHOOSH!' LETS YOUR EYES HEAR SOUND!
skill_films.caption_p2: IN FILM, WE TRIGGER FOLEY SFX AT THE EXACT PEAK OF MOTION:
skill_films.caption_p3: WHEREVER THE ZIGZAG SHARPLY CHANGES DIRECTION (K2 & K3)...
skill_films.caption_p4: ...EARSHOT FIRES A CRISP FOLEY ACCENT RIGHT ON THE BEAT!
skill_films.blurb: Connects comic-book onomatopoeia ('PTU!', 'BANG!', 'WHOOSH!' from McCloud pp. 5-6) to our automated Earshot Foley cues triggered at sharp turns in the motion path.
